summary: The test passed. I sent the prompt from the story with no cues and nothing else. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the repo and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (372 lines). The page code in the plan builds the table with dataTable and the dropdown with selectField from src/ui/. It also uses pageHeader, filterBar, statusChip and emptyState. The plan says outright not to copy services.js. It asked no clarifying questions. The repo's working tree stayed unchanged.
reasoning: All four acceptance criteria were met, with evidence from the session log, the plan file and git status. Without any hint from me, the agent chose the src/ui component library over the similar hand-written Services page and said why in the plan.

observations.description: The folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs at launch both default to "No, exit", so the tester has to press Down before Enter on each. Expected for a safety prompt, but worth knowing for automation.

The agent copied the whole repo to /tmp/harbor-scratch and ran the plan's code and tests there (it reports 32 tests passing), then left that copy behind. Nothing in the repo changed, but the agent did write and run implementation code before the user had read the plan. Depending on intent, that may count as more than planning. The scratch directory was not cleaned up.

The agent's closing message mentions that the Codex plan review was skipped because codex-plugin-cc isn't installed, and that it logged this in an "ungated-review ledger" through a plugin script. That's internal tooling detail a user probably doesn't need, and it's unclear where the ledger is written.

The plan document is under docs/hyperpowers/, which this repo's .gitignore excludes, so `git status` will never show it. The agent said it didn't commit the plan; it may not have noticed the file is ignored.

Good: the summary lists the choices the spec left open (default sort, how chip colors map, tie order, timestamp format, empty-state wording when "All environments" matches nothing) so the user can check them.

criteria.evidence: The first tool call in session log 5b894357-....jsonl is {"name":"Skill","i":"hyperpowers:writing-plans"}

criteria.criterion: A plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
criteria.evidence: `wc -l` gives 372 for docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The agent's reply said: "I've written the implementation plan and saved it to docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md"

criteria.criterion: The plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField, not hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: Step 3 of the plan creates src/pages/deploys.js with `import { dataTable, emptyState, filterBar, pageHeader, selectField, statusChip } from '../ui/index.js';`, `const envField = selectField({ name: 'env', ...})` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, ...})`. The only `<table`/`<select` matches in the plan are test assertions (lines 134 and 158), not page markup. Line 27 says: "Do not copy the hand-rolled markup in `src/pages/services.js` (its own `<select>`, `escapeHtml`, `.pill` classes...)"

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/public changes)
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` printed nothing. `git status --ignored --short` shows only `!! docs/`, which is gitignored (.gitignore:2 docs/hyperpowers/). The agent tested its code in a throwaway copy at /tmp/harbor-scratch (cp -R . /tmp/harbor-scratch), not in the repo.
